causes.label: Door sensor obstruction or misalignment
fix_steps: Inspect door light curtain / safety edge for physical obstructions (debris, worn rubber strips).
Clean the sensor lens with a dry lint-free cloth.
Check sensor alignment — both transmitter and receiver must face each other within ±2 mm.
Use a multimeter to verify the sensor output signal (expect 24 V DC when clear).
Replace door light curtain module if signal is absent after cleaning and alignment.
required_parts: Door light curtain / multi-beam safety sensor

causes.label: Door operator motor or drive belt failure
fix_steps: Power down the elevator at the main disconnect.
Manually open the door and inspect the drive belt for cracks, slack, or breakage.
Check the motor coupling for wear or play.
Measure motor winding resistance (expected 8-12 O per phase for VVVF motors).
Replace belt or motor as indicated; recalibrate door travel limits after replacement.

causes.label: Door controller board malfunction
fix_steps: Check door controller board LEDs for fault indicators.
Inspect ribbon cable and connector pins for corrosion or loose fit.
Perform door controller soft reset (refer to OEM service menu).
Update door controller firmware if a newer version is available.
Replace door controller board if fault persists after reset.

causes.label: Insufficient guide rail lubrication
fix_steps: Inspect guide rail surfaces for dryness, rust streaks, or uneven grease distribution.
Clean rails with a rag dampened with mineral spirits to remove old/hardened grease.
Apply fresh SAE 30 elevator guide rail oil using a brush or auto-lube system.
Check and refill the auto-lubricator reservoir if fitted.
Run the cabin 10 full cycles to distribute lubricant; observe for improvement.

causes.label: VVVF inverter drive parameter mismatch
fix_steps: Connect a laptop to the drive serial port and read current parameter set.
Compare acceleration/deceleration ramp rates with OEM specification sheet.
Adjust S-curve parameters (acceleration jerk rate) — reduce jerk rate by 10% increments until smooth.
Check motor encoder feedback signal for noise or missed pulses (scope the ABZ channels).
Re-tune PI speed controller gains if ride quality does not improve after ramp adjustment.

causes.label: Worn or damaged car roller guides
fix_steps: Visually inspect all four roller guide assemblies for flat spots, cracks, or out-of-round rollers.
Apply hand pressure to each roller and check for radial play greater than 0.5 mm.
Replace worn rollers with OEM-spec polyurethane rollers.
Adjust roller guide spring tension to manufacturer specification after replacement.
Lubricate roller axles with bearing grease and confirm smooth rotation.

causes.label: Motor thermal overload — PTC thermistor triggered
fix_steps: Allow motor to cool for at least 30 minutes with the shaft ventilation fan running.
Check PTC thermistor resistance: should be < 1.5 kO at ambient; > 4 kO indicates trip.
Inspect motor ventilation openings for dust blockage; blow out with compressed air.
Verify that the motor is not undersized for the actual load (check duty cycle logs).
Reset E14 via the drive service menu once motor temperature drops below threshold.

causes.label: Drive heatsink / cooling fan blocked
fix_steps: Power down the drive and remove the front cover.
Inspect the drive heatsink fins and internal fan for dust accumulation.
Use compressed air to clean all fins and vents thoroughly.
Check the cooling fan spins freely and is not seized.
Replace the drive cooling fan if it does not run on power-up.
required_parts: Drive cooling fan (OEM replacement, 48 V DC or 120 V AC as applicable)

causes.label: Encoder cable damaged or loose connection
fix_steps: Power down drive and inspect encoder cable for cuts, kinks, or pinch points along the full run.
Reseat the encoder connector on both the motor end and the drive PG card end.
Measure encoder supply voltage at motor terminal (expect 5 V ±5% or 12 V ±10%).
Scope the A/B channels for clean square wave pulses without noise spikes.
Replace cable with shielded twisted-pair if signal quality is poor; ground the shield at one end only.
required_parts: Shielded encoder cable (5-core, 0.5 mm², per metre)
Encoder connector kit (D-sub 9-pin or M12, per OEM)

causes.label: Encoder optical disk contaminated or damaged
fix_steps: Remove encoder cover (motor end) and inspect the glass/plastic encoder disk.
Carefully wipe the disk with isopropyl alcohol (99%) and a lint-free swab.
Check for cracks or chips in the disk; replace the complete encoder if found.
Verify encoder pulse count per revolution matches drive configuration (e.g. 1024 PPR).
Re-tune drive speed feedback after encoder replacement.

causes.label: Safety chain open — contact not made in safety circuit
fix_steps: Enter inspection mode and use the safety circuit test function to identify the open contact.
Walk the entire safety chain: pit stop switch, overspeed governor, buffer switch, door locks, final limit switches.
With a multimeter set to DC volts, probe across each safety contact in sequence to find the open one.
Inspect the faulty contact for mechanical damage, corrosion, or misalignment.
Clean contacts with contact cleaner spray or replace the defective safety switch.
required_parts: Safety switch (specific to identified contact — door lock, pit stop, or limit switch)
Contact cleaning spray (DeoxIT D5 or equivalent)
Safety relay module (if relay coil failed)

causes.label: Safety relay contacts welded or coil failed
fix_steps: Inspect safety relay coil resistance (typical 200-500 O; open winding = coil failure).
Check for contact weld by measuring continuity in the de-energised state.
Replace the safety relay module with a certified dual-channel safety relay (EN 81 compliant).
After replacement, perform a full safety chain test cycle and log the result.
Update maintenance record and schedule quarterly safety contact inspections.

causes.label: Worn or contaminated brake linings
fix_steps: With the car at the lowest landing and power OFF, access the motor brake assembly.
Measure brake lining thickness — replace if below minimum (typically 3 mm).
Inspect lining surface for oil contamination; if present, identify and fix the oil leak source.
Clean the brake drum/disk with brake cleaner spray if contaminated but not below minimum thickness.
Adjust brake air gap per OEM specification after any lining or spring work.

causes.label: Drive sheave groove wear causing rope slippage
fix_steps: Inspect sheave grooves for uneven wear, cracking, or bottoming of ropes.
Use a sheave gauge tool to measure groove diameter and profile.
If groove depth variance exceeds 1 mm between grooves, re-machine or replace the sheave.
Check all hoist ropes for wear, broken wires, and proper tension.
Re-tension ropes to equal tension within ±5% after sheave work.
required_parts: Hoist rope set (6×19 or 8×19 construction, OEM-spec diameter)

causes.label: Cabin contacting pit buffer spring prematurely
fix_steps: Ride the cabin to the lowest landing and measure compressed clearance above the buffer.
Check if bottom final limit switch is tripping early by recording the exact trigger position.
Adjust final limit switch cam or position per OEM specification.
Inspect buffer spring for corrosion, deformation, or incorrect type.
Re-run full load test and record stopping position.
required_parts: Final limit switch cam adjuster kit
Pit buffer spring (OEM type — oil or spring buffer, per speed class)

causes.label: Floor leveling sensor / vane misalignment
fix_steps: In inspection mode, slowly pass the cabin through each floor and observe leveling sensor LEDs.
Measure the vertical distance from door sill to floor sill at each landing — record deviation.
Adjust the leveling vane position in the shaft (up/down) within ±3 mm.
On microprocessor-controlled systems, use the drive service menu to adjust leveling speed.
Run 5 full-load trips and verify sill-to-sill gap is within ±5 mm at all landings.
required_parts: Leveling sensor (proximity or reed switch, OEM-matched)
Vane bracket and M8 adjustment bolts

causes.label: Drive deceleration ramp too aggressive or too slow
fix_steps: Connect the drive programming tool and navigate to the deceleration distance parameters.
Record the current deceleration distance and compare to installation report baseline.
Increase deceleration distance by 50 mm increments if undershooting.
Decrease deceleration distance by 50 mm increments if overshooting.
Verify changes across all floors at full load and minimum load conditions.

causes.label: Automatic Rescue Device (ARD) battery depleted or failed
fix_steps: Locate the ARD / UPS module in the machine room or control cabinet.
Check the battery status LED — red or amber fault indicator confirms battery failure.
Measure battery terminal voltage under load: SLA 24 V system should hold > 21 V under 5 A draw.
Replace sealed lead-acid or Li-ion battery pack with OEM-specified capacity.
Initiate a manual ARD test cycle per EN 81-20 §5.12.1.5 and log the result.
required_parts: SLA battery pack (24 V / 7 Ah or 12 Ah, OEM-rated)
Battery charge controller (if replacing ARD unit)
ARD module (complete, if board-level repair is not practical)

causes.label: Main line contactor not re-engaging on power restoration
fix_steps: On power restoration, listen for the main contactor closing — silence indicates a fault.
Check the control circuit fuse (typically 6 A or 10 A) on the main board.
Measure coil voltage of the main contactor (should equal the control circuit voltage).
Inspect contactor contacts for pitting or welding; replace if contact resistance > 0.1 O.
Check the phase sequence relay — mis-wired phase order after restoration can inhibit closing.
required_parts: Main line contactor (rated for motor FLA × 1.25)
Control circuit fuse (6 A or 10 A glass fuse, 500 V rated)
Contactor coil (if coil-only replacement is possible)

causes.label: Controller board RAM / NV-RAM corruption after power loss
fix_steps: Perform a cold restart: power OFF for 60 seconds, then power ON and observe initialisation.
If the controller displays a checksum or memory error code, backup current parameters.
Restore factory defaults and re-enter site-specific parameters from the installation record.
Install a surge protector / UPS on the controller circuit to prevent future corruption.
If the problem recurs, replace the controller board NVRAM chip or the full controller board.
required_parts: NVRAM chip (EEPROM / battery-backed SRAM, part number per controller)
Controller board (full, if chip replacement is not viable)
Surge protection device (DIN rail mounted, SPD Type 2)
UPS module for controller circuit (500 VA minimum)

causes.label: Load cell / weighing device calibration drift
fix_steps: Place the cabin empty and zero the load cell via the drive/controller service menu.
Load the cabin with a known test weight (e.g. 50% rated load) and verify display matches.
Recalibrate the overload threshold in the controller to the rated capacity.
Inspect load cell wiring for moisture ingress or frayed cable at the junction box.
Replace load cell if span error exceeds ±5% after calibration attempt.

causes.label: Overload relay wiring fault causing false alarm
fix_steps: Measure the overload relay input signal voltage with the cabin empty.
Check terminal screw tightness and look for loose strands bridging adjacent terminals.
Inspect the overload relay module for visible damage, burn marks, or oxidised contacts.
Perform a relay bypass test to confirm the relay, not the sensor, is at fault.
Replace overload relay module if the sensor checks out but the relay still trips erroneously.
